Hi Joe,

The counts in the object "bwmatrix" were characters instead of integers. Also, your covariates are all considered "siteCovs" by unmarked because they have a single value per site. This code seems to work:

bwmatrix <- read.table(file = "bwmatrix.txt", sep = "\t")
bwFrame <- unmarkedFrameMPois(y=bwmatrix,
    siteCovs=cbind(bwsitecov, bwobscov),
    type="removal")
summary(bwFrame)

# fit models
fm.bw.1 = multinomPois(~1 ~1, bwFrame)

fm.bw.2 = multinomPois(~DOY+MSS ~ Cover, bwFrame)

Hope this helps.

Richard

messages.body_plain:
Hi Kathi,

predict(fm, type="state") returns "lambda" the expected value of "super-population size" (M) at each plot.
In our Ecology paper, we focused on random temporary emigration such that M equals the total number of individuals that use the plot during the season. In that case, "phi" is the probability that an individual is present (on the plot) during a primary period, and the expected value of density is

E[D] = E[N]/A = (lambda*phi)/A.

where N the number of individuals on the plot during a primary period, and A is plot area. This model can be used to model processes other than temporary emigration, in which case the parameters (lambda and phi) will have different interpretations.

If the estimates of M seem too high, it is probably because the estimates of p and/or phi are very low.

Richard

A little background: birds were sampled at 189 point counts 3 times during a season (1 primary period, 3 secondary periods). I'm using 6 landcover classes (% A,B,C...F), % road, and well density and patch size as siteCov. y data (distance) = 189 x 21 matrix                    (site ID in multinomial that corresponds to 7 distance bins x 3 survey periods)

yearlysiteCovs = 189 observations of 7 variables  (site ID, 3 date columns, 3 wind columns)

The abbreviated process (excluding correlation tests, standardizing covariates, etc) looks like this:

## Import distance data (i.e., "y") into R

DIST1 = read.delim(file = "GRSP_SP1_DIST.txt", header=TRUE,sep="\t", colClasses=c("factor","numeric","factor","numeric","numeric"))

## Import covariate (i.e., "siteCovs") data into R

COVS = read.delim("GRSP_COVS.txt",header = TRUE,sep = "\t",colClasses= c(rep("numeric",10),"factor","factor"))

## Import observation covariate (i.e., "yearlySiteCovs") data into R

YRCOVS = read.delim("GRSP_YRCOVS.txt", header = TRUE, sep="\t", colClasses = c("factor","numeric","numeric","numeric","numeric","numeric","numeric"))

## Format distance data into multinomial format

db <- seq(0,140,by=20)
y.dat1 = formatDistData(distData = DIST1, distCol = "dist", transectNameCol="id", dist.breaks=db, occasionCol="round")

## Combine multinomial data in unmarkedframeGDS

umfsp1 <- unmarkedFrameGDS(y = as.matrix(y.dat1), siteCovs = COVS, numPrimary = 1, yearlySiteCovs = YRCOVS, dist.breaks = db, survey = "point", unitsIn = "m")

basedetect$haz.P = gdistsamp(~1,~1,~1, umfsp1, keyfun="hazard", mixture="P", unitsOut="kmsq",output="density",K=200)
basedetect$exp.P = gdistsamp(~1,~1,~1, umfsp1, keyfun="exp", mixture="P", unitsOut="kmsq",output="density",K=200)

data<-read.csv("test.sample.size.csv")

library(unmarked)

# ------------> Set Up piFun and obsToY <------------ #
# piFun
depDoublePiFun <- function(p) {
    M <- nrow(p)
    pi <- matrix(NA, M, 2)
    pi[,1] <- p[,1]
    pi[,2] <- p[,2]*(1-p[,1])
    return(pi)
}

#obsToY
obsToY <- matrix(1, 2, 2)
numPrimary <- 2
obsToY <- kronecker(diag(numPrimary), obsToY)

# ------------> Set Up UMF <------------ #
y<-as.matrix(subset(data,select=c(count_S1_O1,count_S1_O2,count_S2_O1,
    count_S2_O2)))

siteCovs<-data.frame(sitecov=data$sitecov)

obsCovs<-list(obscov = as.matrix(subset(data,select=c(
    obscov_S1_O1,obscov_S1_O2,obscov_S2_O1,obscov_S2_O2))))

umf<-unmarkedFrameGMM(y=y, siteCovs=siteCovs, obsCovs=obsCovs,
    numPrimary=numPrimary, obsToY=obsToY, piFun="depDoublePiFun")
summary(umf)

# ------------> Fit Models <------------ #
m1 <- gmultmix(~1,~1,~1, data=umf, control=list(trace=TRUE))
m2 <- gmultmix(~1,~1,~obscov, data=umf, control=list(trace=TRUE))
m3  <- gmultmix(~1,~1,~sitecov, data=umf,control=list(trace=TRUE))

fms <- fitList(        "(.)" = m1,
                "(obscov)" = m2,
                "(sitecovs)" = m3)
(ms <- modSel(fms))
